Internships.job_description_summary: Interns on CrowdStrike's Intel Automation team pick a project in data science/AI, platform engineering, software engineering, or security research (binary analysis, vulnerability research, threat intelligence). They help build and run the systems behind the intelligence pipeline, including AI-assisted workflows with verification and monitoring. The posting asks for a penultimate-year CS/Engineering/Math student with Python, Go, Rust or JavaScript/TypeScript, Linux, git and CI/CD experience, plus demonstrated use of AI agents.

Interns join CrowdStrike's Counter Adversary Operations automation team to build AI agents and automated workflows that help Elite analysts investigate threats. Day to day they write and test Python integrations using REST APIs and JSON, evaluate agents for accuracy, and shadow analysts. It is a Launch program role for first- or second-year students in Computer Science, Cyber Security or a similar degree.

The intern joins the Managed Service Provider product team at Rubrik, a cyber resilience and data security company, reporting to the Director of Product Management, Platform. They analyze MSP workflows and competitors, write problem statements and PRDs, and validate ideas with MSP customers and engineering. Candidates should be MBA or Master's students finishing Dec 2027 or Spring 2028 who are comfortable with system architecture, APIs and cloud infrastructure.

The intern supports the Rubrik Cloud Vault team, which protects customers' critical application data for recovery during cyber and disaster incidents. They analyze customer use cases and the market, write PRDs, and work with engineering, design and go-to-market teams. Candidates should be Master's or MBA students finishing Dec 2027 or Spring 2028 with exposure to technical systems, cloud infrastructure and APIs.

The intern works on a defined research project at the intersection of AI, cybersecurity and computer systems at Horizon3 (autonomous pentesting). They read papers, build prototypes, run experiments, and work with security data such as attack paths, telemetry and cloud environments alongside researchers and attack engineers. The posting asks for a CS or related student with strong fundamentals and interest in systems security or machine learning.

Projects.title: Python Security Log Analyzer
Projects.description: Build a command-line tool that parses simulated authentication logs (JSON lines), flags brute-force and password-spray patterns, and enriches suspicious IPs from a simulated threat-intel feed. Practiced in the style of a security analyst's investigation support work.
Projects.final_deliverable: A GitHub-ready repository with the analyzer script, simulated log generator, sample findings report, and README.

Projects.title: Mini SOAR Alert Triage Playbook
Projects.description: Build an automated triage workflow that pulls alerts as JSON from a mock REST API, enriches and scores them, and routes them to close, escalate or investigate, mirroring analyst automation work.
Projects.final_deliverable: A repository with the playbook code, mock alert API, test cases, and a short write-up of triage rules and accuracy.

Projects.title: Cloud Attack Path Mapper
Projects.description: Model a simulated cloud environment (identities, roles, network rules) as a graph, find attack paths to critical assets, and rank them by risk with suggested control fixes.
Projects.final_deliverable: A report and repository with the environment model, path-finding script, risk-ranked findings, and an attack path diagram.

Milestones.title: Explore and simulate the authentication data
Milestones.instructions: Write a script that generates about 5,000 simulated login events as JSON lines (timestamp, user, source_ip, result, method) including a few planted attacks: one brute-force burst, one password-spray, and one login from a rare IP. Load the file, count events by user, IP and result, and note what normal traffic looks like.
Milestones.deliverable: data/auth_logs.jsonl, generator script, and a short notes file listing baseline statistics
Milestones.resource_title: Python docs: json - JSON encoder and decoder

Milestones.title: Build the analyzer
Milestones.instructions: Create analyzer.py with a command-line interface that reads a log file and applies detection rules: N failed logins from one IP in a time window, one IP failing against many users, and success after many failures. Print findings as JSON. Run and test it on Linux or WSL.
Milestones.deliverable: analyzer.py with CLI flags and at least three detection rules
Milestones.resource_title: Python docs: argparse - Parser for command-line options

Milestones.title: Investigate the findings
Milestones.instructions: For each finding, build a short timeline, enrich the source IP against a simulated threat-intel list, and map the behavior to a known technique. Write a one-paragraph verdict and recommended response per finding.
Milestones.deliverable: findings_report.md with timelines, enrichment results, and recommended actions

Milestones.title: Publish a GitHub-ready deliverable
Milestones.instructions: Clean the code, add a README (purpose, install, usage, sample output, detection rules, limitations), add a .gitignore, make small descriptive commits, and push to a public repository.
Milestones.deliverable: Public GitHub repository link with README, code, sample data, and report
Milestones.resource_title: GitHub Docs: About the repository README file
